A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same expected-transformer approach to mean-field dynamics, despite the changed title. Their complete text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support comparison.

before.justification: Section 5 and Figures 1–3 report original Cucker-Smale simulations and experiments approximating two-layer neural-network training dynamics.

after.justification: Section 3 retains the original simulations and adds comparative results on Cucker-Smale and real fish-milling data. Section 4.3 also reports a new approximation-error analysis.

M1.justification: The transformer architecture, expected-transformer construction, and mean-squared-error vector-field learning procedure are retained. The architecture definitions move from Section 3.1 to Appendix D; additional training specifications do not establish a changed proposed method.

E1.justification: v2 adds real fish-milling data spanning 5,000 time steps, with incomplete observations and changing particle identities/counts. This substantially extends coverage beyond v1's synthetic Cucker-Smale and neural-network training examples, both of which remain.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds evaluated cylindrical networks, GraphConv and TransformerConv with 3- and 20-neighbor graphs, plus FNN and kernel-regression baselines on Cucker-Smale only. v1 contains no corresponding architectural benchmark; its comparisons with true dynamics and gradient-based training remain.

E3.justification: The added benchmark study introduces validation-selected comparisons and 3-/20-neighbor graph controls. Figure 4 adds Gibbs sampling over five fixed positions and an 11-by-11 velocity grid. v2 also reports 30 simulated Cucker-Smale particles instead of ten, although Figure 3 still captions ten; this inconsistency prevents establishing whether that experiment was rerun.

E4.justification: Section 4.3 and Figure 4 add a focused diagnostic comparing sampled expected-transformer errors with the theoretical bound across position/velocity settings. The trajectory and neural-network parameter-error analyses already present in Figures 1–3 are retained.

E5.justification: v2 specifies five trials per hyperparameter configuration and introduces plus/minus uncertainty entries in Table 1, without defining the uncertainty statistic. The existing 100-trial median and interquartile-range reporting in Figures 1–2 remains unchanged.

E6.justification: Table 1 adds substantial comparative results: the transformer has the lowest reported MSE on both Cucker-Smale (1.9e-6) and fish milling (2.2e-2). Figure 4 newly reports maximum sampled error 0.025 against a stated bound of at least 0.05. Figures 1–3 retain their earlier results.

T1.justification: v2 replaces Wp-based regularity with W1 regularity, removes the explicit smoothness assumption, and revises approximation bounds and their proofs. Theorem 4.12 and Appendix B add an existence-and-uniqueness argument using a cutoff, replacing v1's Assumption 2. The dynamics theorem is reformulated in W1, although inconsistent p/Wp expressions remain elsewhere.

C1.justification: v2 adds superiority over alternative architectures as its first main contribution and broadens the abstract's empirical scope to fish milling. v1's three listed contributions concern the expected-transformer construction and approximation theory; those central theoretical objectives remain.

C2.justification: v2 interprets the reported transfer from 20 training particles to 30 simulation particles as evidence of learning the interaction kernel. It also replaces v1's explicit short-horizon qualification with discussion of approximation over a prescribed finite interval, while retaining the exponential error-growth warning.

D1.justification: Appendix E newly supplies hyperparameter ranges, optimizer and scheduler choices, batch sizes, and epoch budgets. Section 3 expands neural-network data-generation details and adds a code-access link. These substantially improve documentation, although v1's BDF solver specification and 16,834-sample count are omitted.

R1.justification: The broad neural-network/PDE approximation background is replaced by a focused Section 5 comparison of measure roles, architectures, and guarantees. v2 adds positioning against Kratsios and Furuya (2025), alongside new citations for probabilistic transformers, fish data, GNN baselines, and attention regularity, while removing much of the earlier general background.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, and experimental narrative are extensively revised. Experiments move ahead of theory, notation becomes an introduction subsection, architecture definitions move to Appendix D, and related work becomes a dedicated later section. This is substantial restructuring beyond the added scientific content.

P2.justification: v2 switches the main text to a two-column conference layout, adds Table 1 and the five-panel heatmap Figure 4, and substantially resizes and relocates Figures 1–3. The retained plots preserve their underlying results.

improvement.justification: Table 1 supplies architectural comparisons and real-data validation absent from v1, while Appendix E substantially improves reproducibility information. These materially strengthen the paper's empirical support and auditability. The added existence-and-uniqueness argument also addresses a previously assumed condition, although theoretical consistency remains imperfect. The ambiguous '80-20-20' split, conflicting particle counts, and residual W1/Wp expressions limit confidence but do not outweigh the substantial gains in evidence and documentation.
